title: Accounts Receivable
subtitle: Customer invoices, receipts and module receivables
summary: Accounts Receivable keeps everything customers owe the club: invoices entered here (stabling, farrier ...) and every charge raised in another module, imported automatically from posted accounting events. Receipts, cheques that must clear and reversals complete the picture, reconciled to GL 1200 and 1210.

sections.title: Accounts Receivable database architecture · Visual ERD
sections.intro: The financial_ar MySQL schema contains three domain tables and seven declared foreign keys. Every invoice has line items and can have multiple receipts; each line points to a General Ledger revenue account.

sections.title: What Accounts Receivable means in everyday business
paragraphs: Accounts Receivable (AR) is the list of money that customers owe the club. A customer may have already received a service—horse registration, membership, racing entry or a restaurant charge—but may pay later. AR records exactly who owes what, why, and when it is due.

The ar_invoice is the bill sent to the customer; ar_invoice_line explains the individual charges and tax; ar_receipt records money received against the bill. Recording a receipt is not the same as the bank clearing the funds.

The club can consolidate charges originating in multiple business modules into one customer-facing financial view. source_module records where an invoice originated; the actual inbound event capture, idempotency and import processing are architectural mechanisms outside these three tables.

sections.title: Worked example: four services, one customer account
paragraphs: Illustrative example: A horse owner is charged $500 for registration, $250 for race entry, $150 for a licence and $100 for stabling. The club must know these are charges to the same enterprise_core.party, even though four business modules generated them.

The combined outstanding amount is $1,000 if none has been paid. When the customer pays $400, the remaining balance is $600, assuming the receipt is valid and applied to those charges. The AR system must prevent a repeated import or repeated receipt from accidentally changing that balance twice.

The physical schema stores source_module on each invoice and does not itself define an invoice-to-source-event unique key. Correct source-event deduplication and any cross-module aggregation rules therefore require an explicit integration or application design.

sections.title: From a business event to cash and the books
items: 1. Business service creates a charge. Horse Registry, Membership, Hospitality or another module records a billable event.
2. Finance imports the receivable. The AR integration identifies the same customer party and prevents the same source event from creating duplicates.
3. Invoice and lines are recorded. The header names the customer, currency, dates, source module and total; lines identify charges, tax and revenue accounts.
4. GL recognises the transaction. Journal references create an auditable bridge between the AR subledger and company accounts.
5. Customer pays. A receipt is recorded, then moves through clearance or reversal handling.
6. AR reconciles. Outstanding balances, ageing and the relevant GL control accounts must agree.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The AR import runs every minute over posted outbox events. A reference table (AR_IMPORT_EVENT) says what each module event means: INVOICE (create an invoice), SETTLE (pay it, e.g. a membership receipt), ADD (add tax to an invoice), CREDIT (an event booking cancelled).
Imported invoices are accounted by source: the module's own event already hit the GL, so AR does not post them again. That avoids double counting while still giving one customer view.
Anything the import cannot apply (no party, settlement above the balance) is SKIPPED with a reason and shown as an exception.

terms.definition: DRAFT → POSTED → PART_PAID → PAID, or VOID; due date from TERMS_DAYS.
Money received into a bank account. Cheques stay PENDING until cleared; a bounced cheque is a reversal.
An invoice created from another module's posted event.
The GL entry came from the originating module, so AR does not post it again.
